deviations.description: similarity: test predictions for pairs with a sample without training response
deviations.explanation: A test pair with a sample that has no response in training. v2 fits the factors on the samples of the training batch only and predicts the training mean for a sample or a drug it has no factor for (documented in `docs/explanation/literature_models.rst`: if either is unknown the prediction is the mean). 1.6.1 factorizes every sample of the feature dataset (`np.unique(cell_line_input.identifiers)`): such a sample gets latent factors from the similarity term alone, and a sample that is absent gets the training mean as its latent *vector*, so the prediction is `u . mean` (`K * mean^2` when the drug is unknown too).

findings: Fixed (v2): SRMF fitted in the first-seen order of the entities, 1.6.1 in sorted id order (`np.unique`). The initial factors are drawn row by row from the seeded generator, so the order decides the start point of the whole optimization. v2 now sorts samples and drugs by id before the solver; variant `fit_order` compares the factors in stored order, and the harness no longer reorders the arrays.

The solver is the 1.6.1 one and agrees to rounding when both sides factorize the same samples and drugs (variants `similarity` and `plain`): same seeded `default_rng` initialization, same alternating updates, same stopping rule. The response pivot, the Jaccard similarity of the fingerprints and the Pearson correlation of the expression are identical.

1.6.1 is transductive in the sample set: `train` factorizes `np.unique(cell_line_input.identifiers)`, i.e. every sample of the dataset, also those that occur only in validation or test pairs, and the sample similarity is computed over all of them. v2 factorizes the samples of the training batch. The drugs are the same in practice (every drug is trained). Variant `transductive` shows the effect: sample set, similarity, initial factors and all factors differ.

Prediction fallback: 1.6.1 fills the latent vector of an unknown sample or drug with the training mean (`np.full((n, K), mean)`), so its prediction is `u . mean` or `K * mean^2`; v2 returns the training mean (documented). With a transductive sample set 1.6.1 rarely hits the fallback for samples.

The v2 defaults (K 45, lambda_l 0.01, lambda_d 0, lambda_c 0.01, max_iter 50, seed 1) are the 1.6.1 ones; `n_features` (1036) is in both hyperparameter lists and is not used by either solver. The preset reads `raw[gene_expression]` with no gene list (1.6.1: `gene_list=None`, every column). The case sets all hyperparameters explicitly.
